chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: While the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was in his chambers with one of his wives, and with him was a spindle which he was turning, when he saw two eyes peeking at him. So he said: 'If I knew that you would remain fixed for me, I would arise until I blind you.' So I said: 'Shall we do the like of this, if the like of this is done to us?' He said: 'If it is hidden from you (i.e., you are not seen), then do it.'

key_terms.أَبْخَسَكَ: I will blind you (literally: I will make you lose your eyes)
key_terms.مَغَازِلُ: spindles (plural of mighzal, used for spinning thread)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on peeking at someone in their private chamber according to the Prophet (SAWW)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the principle of *qisas* (retaliatory justice) regarding the eyes, specifically in cases where the perpetrator is not immediately identifiable or the victim cannot easily prove the offense. The Prophet’s (SAW) use of the spindle (*maghazil*) highlights the domestic context of this privacy violation, while the Imam’s confirmation extends the permissibility of blinding the observer to situations where the act is concealed (*khafiya*), establishing a legal precedent for reciprocal punishment in privacy breaches.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Al Mukhtar, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘While Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was in his<sup>saww</sup> chamber with one of his<sup>saww</sup> wives, and with him<sup>asws</sup> was a spindle of his<sup>saww</sup> which he<sup>saww</sup> was turning, when he<sup>saww</sup> saw two eye peeking at him<sup>saww</sup>. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘If I<sup>saww</sup> knew that you would remain there for me<sup>saww</sup>, I<sup>saww</sup> would arise until I<sup>saww</sup> blind you’. So I said, ‘Shall we do the like of this, if the like of this is done with us?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it is hidden for you (you are not seen), so do it’.
